# Fixture sources (logs domain)

Every fixture is either real output captured on the development machines or
assembled from real log lines published in the bug reports and articles
below. Timestamps, host names and serials were changed to fit the test clock
(2026-10-01 09:00 UTC unless the test says otherwise); message text was kept
verbatim unless noted.

## Real output (captured while writing this domain)

| File | What | How |
|---|---|---|
| `wsl_kernel.txt`, `wsl_kernel_match.txt`, `wsl_units.txt`, `wsl_boots.txt`, `wsl_kdump.txt` | `logs.kernel`, `logs.kernel_match`, `logs.units`, `logs.boots`, `logs.kdump` from `collect/linux/60-logs.sh` | Ubuntu 26.04 under WSL2 (systemd 259, persistent journal), run as root, 2026-10-02. Other agents' tests on the same WSL had created md arrays (`md90`, `md91`), a bond (`bond9`) and broken ext4 images on loop devices, so these are real kernel/mdadm messages. Host name replaced by `devbox`; 736 repeated `dxgkio_query_adapter_info` lines removed from `wsl_kernel.txt`. |
| `wsl_kernlog_rfc3339.txt` | `/var/log/kern.log` written by rsyslog in RFC 3339 format | Same WSL, `grep ' kernel: ' /var/log/kern.log`, filtered to bond/md/ext4 lines; header line added as the collector writes it. |
| `real_win_events.json`, `real_win_summary.json`, `real_win_boots.json` | `logs.win_events`, `logs.win_summary`, `logs.win_boots` from `collect/windows/60-logs.ps1` | Windows 10 22H2 (build 19045) dev machine, not elevated, 2026-10-02. Contains a real blue screen (0xBE + EventLog 6008), a flaky USB disk (UASPStor 129, disk 51/153, Ntfs 55/98/140) and volmgr 161. Computer and user names replaced. |

| `real_win_physical.json`, `real_win_diskdrive.json`, `real_win_volume.json`, `real_win_meta.json` | `disk.win_physical`, `disk.win_diskdrive`, `filesystem.win_volume` (disk/filesystem collectors) and `logs.win_meta` | Same Windows 10 laptop, not elevated, 2026-10-02, collected right after `real_win_events.json`: the USB disk that logged the disk 51/153 and NTFS 55/98/140 events (PhysicalDrive1, volume G:) is no longer attached, so neither appears. |

## Copied verbatim from public pages

| File | Origin |
|---|---|
| `linux_ghes_pcie_ibm.txt` | The first 26 `[Hardware Error]` lines of the dmesg excerpt on IBM support page "IBM ESS: IBM Elastic Storage System 3500 may see PCIe AER errors in the dmesg" (https://www.ibm.com/support/pages/ibm-ess-ibm-elastic-storage-system-3500-may-see-pcie-aer-errors-dmesg): a corrected GHES PCIe record whose sections carry `device_id: 0000:02:00.0`. Collector header lines added. |
| `linux_usb_dmesg.txt` | Lines `117.07`–`117.55` (USB reset, `sd 6:0:0:0: [sdb]` with sense data on separate lines, `end_request: I/O error, dev sdb`, `Buffer I/O error on device sdb1`) from LKML "Re: Buffer I/O error after s2ram with usb storage" (https://lkml.iu.edu/hypermail/linux/kernel/1404.3/02964.html). The three attach lines at 4–5 s are synthesised from the same kernel generation's format strings (`USB Mass Storage device detected`, 3.x `scsi%d : usb-storage %s`, `Attached SCSI disk`) for host 6; the 4.x+ form (`scsi host11: usb-storage 2-1.6:1.0`, `[sdb] Attached SCSI removable disk`) used inline in `TestLinuxUSBRemovable` is verbatim from https://bbs.archlinux.org/viewtopic.php?id=207447. |

Other inline lines in `review_test.go` follow kernel format strings: btrfs `(device %s: state %s)` (fs/btrfs/messages.c, Linux >= 6.1), NVMe `%s(0x%x) @ LBA %llu, %u blocks, %s (sct 0x%x / sc 0x%x)` with the status names of drivers/nvme/host/constants.c, AER `PCIe Bus Error: severity=...` (drivers/pci/pcie/aer.c), Kernel-Power 41 event data order from https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/troubleshoot/windows-client/performance/event-id-41-restart (BugcheckCode, BugcheckParameter1-4, SleepInProgress, PowerButtonTimestamp).

## Assembled from published log lines

| File | Lines and origin |
|---|---|
| `linux_failing_match.txt` | ATA exception / failed command / `hard resetting link` / `SATA link up`: Red Hat Bugzilla 1084928 (https://bugzilla.redhat.com/show_bug.cgi?id=1084928). `Sense Key : Medium Error`, `Add. Sense: Unrecovered read error`, `error: { UNC }`, `status: { DRDY ERR }`, `blk_update_request: I/O error, dev sda, sector 658332184 op 0x0:(READ)`, `XFS (dm-0): metadata I/O error in "xfs_imap_to_bp+0x51/0x90 [xfs]"`: Fedora Discussion 76633 (https://discussion.fedoraproject.org/t/blk-update-request-i-o-error-dev-sda-xfs-dm-0-metadata-i-o-error/76633). `FAILED Result: hostbyte=DID_OK driverbyte=DRIVER_SENSE`, `op 0x9:(WRITE_ZEROES)` I/O error, `Buffer I/O error on dev ..., async page read`: Launchpad bug 1856434 (https://bugs.launchpad.net/bugs/1856434). NVMe `I/O 448 QID 5 timeout, aborting/reset controller`, `Device not ready; aborting reset, CSTS=0x1`, `Removing after probe failure status: -19`, `I/O error, dev nvme1n1`, `Buffer I/O error on dev nvme1n1p1, lost async page write`, `EXT4-fs error (device nvme1n1p1): __ext4_find_entry:1535`, `EXT4-fs (nvme1n1p1): I/O error while writing superblock`: Launchpad bug 1910866 (https://bugs.launchpad.net/bugs/1910866). EDAC `HANDLING MCE MEMORY ERROR`, `Machine check events logged`, `EDAC MC1: 1 CE memory scrubbing error on CPU_SrcID#1_Ha#0_Chan#1_DIMM#0`: Wikimedia Phabricator T227867 (https://phabricator.wikimedia.org/T227867); the parenthesised detail after the DIMM label follows the sb_edac format string (drivers/edac/sb_edac.c). AER lines (`Multiple Uncorrected (Non-Fatal) error received`, vfio-pci `UnsupReq`, `device recovery successful`, mpt3sas `severity=Corrected, type=Physical Layer`, `RxErr`): Unraid forum thread 103901 (https://forums.unraid.net/topic/103901-solved-aer-pcie-bus-errors/). Thermal throttle: format of Red Hat solution 134973 / kernel `arch/x86/kernel/cpu/mce/therm_throt.c`. Synthesised from kernel format strings (no single public log found): `ata1.00: ATA-9: ...` (drivers/ata/libata-core.c), `ata5: SATA link down (SStatus 0 SControl 300)` (libata-core.c), igb/e1000e `NIC Link is Down` (drivers/net/ethernet/intel), `watchdog: BUG: soft lockup - CPU#2 stuck for 23s!` (kernel/watchdog.c), `INFO: task ... blocked for more than 120 seconds.` (kernel/hung_task.c), OOM killer lines (mm/oom_kill.c), `traps: ... general protection fault ip:` (arch/x86/kernel/traps.c), `ACPI: LAPIC_NMI` and an `ACPI Error: AE_NOT_FOUND` line (drivers/acpi), `EXT4-fs ... Remounting filesystem read-only` (fs/ext4/super.c), `md/raid1:md0: Disk failure on sdb1, disabling device.` / `Operation continuing on 1 devices.` (drivers/md/raid1.c). |
| `linux_units.txt` | smartd messages follow smartd.cpp format strings (https://github.com/smartmontools/smartmontools/blob/master/smartmontools/smartd.cpp): `Device: %s, %d Currently unreadable (pending) sectors`, `Offline uncorrectable sectors`, `No more ... warning condition reset`, `SMART Prefailure Attribute: ... changed from`, `ATA error count increased from`, `FAILED SMART self-check. BACK UP DATA NOW!`, `Critical Warning (0x04): Reliability`, `Temperature %d Celsius reached limit of %d Celsius`. The pending/uncorrectable wording also appears verbatim in https://www.linuxquestions.org/questions/linux-hardware-18/smartd-currently-unreadable-pending-sectors-errors-4175659756/. mdadm `Fail event detected on md device /dev/md0, component device /dev/sdb1`, `DegradedArray event`, `RebuildFinished event`: mdadm Monitor.c format (the real WSL capture shows the `mdadm: ` prefix newer versions add). |
| `linux_ghes.txt` | APEI/GHES record layout from drivers/firmware/efi/cper.c and drivers/acpi/apei/ghes.c (`{N}[Hardware Error]: event severity: corrected`, `section_type: memory error`, `section_type: PCIe error`). MCE bank line format from arch/x86/kernel/cpu/mce/core.c (`CPU %d: Machine Check: %Ld Bank %d: %016Lx`); status `be00000000800400` (UC set) is the classic example in mcelog's documentation. `Memory failure: %#lx: recovery action for %s: %s` from mm/memory-failure.c. |
| `rhel7_messages_match.txt` | RHEL-style `/var/log/messages` lines (syslog timestamps without a year, across New Year) plus a `dmesg -T` block. megaraid_sas `FW in FAULT state` / `resetting fusion adapter` (drivers/scsi/megaraid/megaraid_sas_fusion.c), `rejecting I/O to offline device` and `Device offlined - not ready after error recovery` (drivers/scsi/scsi_lib.c, scsi_error.c), `XFS (sdc1): Log I/O Error (0x2) detected at xlog_ioend_work ... Shutting down filesystem` and `Please unmount the filesystem and rectify the problem(s)` (fs/xfs/xfs_fsops.c), `NMI watchdog: BUG: soft lockup` (RHEL 7 wording), `Sense Key : Hardware Error [current] [descriptor]` / `Internal target failure` (drivers/scsi/constants.c). |
| `dmesg_plain.txt` | Plain `dmesg` (seconds since boot). libata `SError: { UnrecovData Handshk }`, `error: { ICRC ABRT }`, `SError: { BadCRC }` (libata-eh.c), bnxt_en `TX timeout detected, starting reset task!` (drivers/net/ethernet/broadcom/bnxt), `NETDEV WATCHDOG: eno2 (tg3): transmit queue 0 timed out` (net/sched/sch_generic.c), `Uhhuh. NMI received for unknown reason 2d on CPU 0.` / `Dazed and confused, but trying to continue` (arch/x86/kernel/nmi.c), `Watchdog detected hard LOCKUP on cpu 5` (kernel/watchdog_perf.c), `BUG: unable to handle kernel NULL pointer dereference` (arch/x86/mm/fault.c). |
| `boots_unclean.txt` | `journalctl --list-boots` (old format with an em dash between first and last entry) and the CentOS 7 clean-shutdown tail (`Reached target Shutdown`, `Starting Reboot...`, `systemd-shutdown[1]: Sending SIGTERM`, `systemd-journal[483]: Journal stopped`) from Red Hat article 2642741, "How to distinguish between a crash and a graceful reboot" (https://access.redhat.com/articles/2642741). The unclean and incomplete tails are synthesised. |
| `last_ungraceful.txt`, `last_graceful.txt` | `last -Fxn2 shutdown reboot` outputs (two `reboot` lines in a row = no clean shutdown) from Red Hat article 2642741; year-less `last -x` format from https://kb.ipserverone.com/knowledge-base/reading-last-command-output-to-identify-unexpected-reboots-on-linux/. The `- crash` reboot line follows util-linux last.c. |
| `kdump.txt` | Collector format of `logs.kdump`; directory names follow RHEL kdump (`/var/crash/127.0.0.1-<date>/vmcore`, `vmcore-dmesg.txt`) and Debian kdump-tools (`/var/crash/<stamp>/dump.<stamp>`, `dmesg.<stamp>`). |
| `win_hw_events.json`, `win_boots.json` | Shaped exactly like the collector output (compare `real_win_events.json`). Provider names and IDs: WHEA-Logger 17/18/19/46/47 (https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/answers/questions/1329135/ and https://www.thewindowsclub.com/fix-whea-logger-fatal-hardware-and-event-id-errors), Kernel-Power 41 BugcheckCode (decimal) and PowerButtonTimestamp properties, including the sample timestamp 131728546170882432 as property 6 after SleepInProgress (https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/troubleshoot/windows-client/performance/event-id-41-restart), WER-SystemErrorReporting 1001 property 0 (format as in the real capture), disk 7/52, storahci 129, e1dexpress 27 "Network link is disconnected" (https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/answers/questions/2607696/), Kernel-Processor-Power 37, NDIS 10400, User32 1074. Two messages are in Vietnamese on purpose (the analysis must not depend on message text); their wording is ours, not Microsoft's. |
